answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to place a refundable bond in a scarce on-chain token, then slash it if the agent is caught double-claiming rewards or violating a verifiable task rule. Rewards accrue only after independent agents attest to useful work, with attestations weighted by their own bonded stake; a cluster of fresh accounts cannot simply echo one another or whisper approval into existence. To capture more rewards, an attacker must lock up more capital, pay transaction costs, and risk losing the bond, so a swarm of hollow identities becomes expensive rather than free.
